name: Objectivism
summary: Objectivism is Ayn Rand's philosophy of reason, rational self-interest and individual rights. It holds that each person is an end in himself, that no one may initiate force against another, and that the only proper government is a minimal one protecting rights, under a regime of unregulated laissez-faire capitalism. It rejects faith, altruism, collectivism and anarchism.
scope: The philosophy as set out by Ayn Rand (The Virtue of Selfishness, Capitalism: The Unknown Ideal, Atlas Shrugged) and systematized by Leonard Peikoff, as presented by the Ayn Rand Institute and Atlas Society. It excludes libertarianism and anarcho-capitalism, which Rand rejected. Many social and foreign-policy answers are inferred from principles and carry low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Rights are negative claims to non-interference, so state-guaranteed medical care would force some to serve others and is rejected.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Objectivists oppose minimum-wage laws as interference in voluntary exchange.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rand held that the value of work and goods is set by voluntary trade, and that government controls cause the harms blamed on markets.

public-ownership.rationale: Only laissez-faire capitalism with private ownership respects rights; the state should be separated from the economy.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Objectivists oppose involuntary taxation and enforced redistribution, so higher taxes on any group to fund more state activity are opposed.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of coercion: voluntary unions are acceptable but Objectivists oppose compulsory-bargaining privileges and see collective claims skeptically.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Rand defended full, unregulated laissez-faire capitalism and held that regulation corrupts both state and market.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is derived from the right to life and is central to Objectivist politics.

cut-welfare.rationale: State welfare is enforced redistribution that Rand rejected, leaving the needy to voluntary charity; the dependency framing is secondary.

worker-ownership.rationale: Ownership arrangements should be left to voluntary contract, but a collective-ownership ideal is rejected as collectivism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred: government exists to protect rights against aggressors, but Objectivists oppose treating innocent citizens as suspects.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the principle that force may be used only against those who initiate it, which implies consenting adult conduct is not the state's business.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Objectivists oppose all censorship, including legal limits on opinion.

strong-leader.rationale: Government must act under objective law with delegated powers; dictatorship is classed as statism.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: the right of self-defense follows from the right to life, so strict limits on peaceful ownership are disfavored.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police and army are proper government functions and Objectivists favor a firm defense, but authority is confined to rights protection.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the non-initiation principle: voluntary adult exchange is not a matter for the law.

state-harmful.rationale: Rand rejected anarchism and held government is a necessary agent for protecting rights.

decide-locally.rationale: Objectivism cares about objective, rights-protecting law rather than the level of government at which it is made.

rehabilitation.rationale: Objectivists treat justice as retributive, including punishment of those who initiate force.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected duty to groups and tradition as authority; family is a private matter, not a societal foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from individual rights and equal treatment under law; Objectivists do not oppose it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Rand championed legal abortion as a woman's right over her own body.

more-religion-public.rationale: Objectivists reject faith as a source of knowledge and oppose religious symbols and initiatives in government.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Objectivists oppose racism but regard affirmative action as legal racism and reject group claims.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed directly; Rand rejected feminism's collectivism but also biological determinism of mind.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Inferred: Rand valued individual choice over inherited collective tradition, and Objectivists say immigration does not destroy culture.

gradual-change.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected conservatism as defending an unprincipled status quo and called for principled change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Objectivist writers hold that immigration restrictions violate individual rights and favor open borders.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred: world bodies would pool power beyond rights-protecting governments and are associated with altruism and statism.

free-trade.rationale: Rand named abolition of tariffs and trade barriers as the essence of capitalism's foreign policy.

nation-first.rationale: Rand wanted a self-interested but trading foreign policy, so adherents would not endorse either side of this framing.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Altruism is said to justify intervention abroad, which Objectivists reject; force is justified for national self-defense.

open-borders.rationale: ARI-aligned writers favor open immigration in a free society, though borders matter for a rights-protecting state.

limit-growth.rationale: Objectivists see production and industrial progress as virtuous and reject environmentalist limits.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Objectivists oppose most government environmental regulation as forced moral views.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from Rand's celebration of reason and industrial production.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from support for industrial energy production and opposition to environmental restrictions.

revolution-justified.rationale: Inferred: a people may resist a government that violates rights, though Rand urged opposing unjust law through ideas.

experts-over-public.rationale: Objectivists reject rule by officials and by majorities alike; objective law, not experts, constrains power.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning violates individual rights and is statism.

socialized-markets.rationale: Private ownership is part of capitalism's justification; public or collective ownership is rejected even with markets.

land-value-tax.rationale: Involuntary taxation is opposed, and the land tax is no exception.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Property rights extend to disposal of property, and Objectivists oppose compulsory taxation beyond a minimal state.

basic-income.rationale: Rand rejected the unearned and enforced redistribution.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: In "The Roots of War" Rand writes that capitalism's foreign policy is free trade, meaning the abolition of trade barriers and protective tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The state should be separated from the economy; Rand attacked the aristocracy of pull and government favors.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Rand defended big business and held that how property is distributed should result from voluntary trade, not policy.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage labor and trade are core to capitalism as Rand defended it.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from separating state and economics, which includes money; Rand's advocates favor gold-based money, not opened here.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognized bodies setting wages and prices are statism.

one-party-rule.rationale: Rule by a party guided by an ideology violates rights; dictatorship is statism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Inferred: government legitimacy comes from the consent of the governed, not heredity.

democracy-best.rationale: Unlimited democracy is classed as statism; the limits on government are rights, not majorities.

direct-votes.rationale: Majority rule over rights is rejected; government is bound to objective law.

workers-councils.rationale: Rights-protecting government under objective law, not class-based bodies, is the basis for power.

right-to-secede.rationale: Individual rights, not regional claims, matter; a free region might secede but an unfree one would not be endorsed.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rand rejected rule by an elite; legitimate government acts as the citizens' agent.

political-violence-never.rationale: Force is justified in retaliation against those who initiate it, so political violence is not never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: Rand cast the warrior as the antagonist of the trader and said capitalism alone bans force.

separate-church-state.rationale: Objectivists want strict separation and oppose faith-based initiatives and religious symbols in government.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Faith and mysticism are rejected as sources of knowledge; law should follow objective rights.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rand rejected anarchism; private marketed courts and police would be a miscarriage of justice.

military-superiority.rationale: A firm, assertive defense of free nations is part of the ARI reading of Rand.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rand calls racism the lowest, most crudely primitive form of collectivism, because it gives political significance to a person's genetic lineage.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rand held that interests of rational individuals do not conflict and rejected Marxism; ideas, not class, drive history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Rights are to freedom of action, not results.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Collective and group rights are rejected, and property rests on individual rights.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred: collective guilt and group claims are rejected.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred: group identity is not a legitimate basis for politics.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rand proudly advocated rational selfishness as the moral standard.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rand held that no one owes the community a sacrifice and that the individual is an end in himself.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Objectivism holds value exists only relative to living beings and nature has no value apart from human purposes.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred: coercive population control violates rights and Objectivists see human life as the standard of value.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Rand defended industrial civilization and called environmentalism an anti-industrial revolution.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Inferred from admiration for production and reason; institutions are not valued in themselves.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from freedom of action over one's own life and body.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred: government is a limited agent under objective law, not a decision-maker over life.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of private property and individual rights against the state.

restore-past-order.rationale: Rand attacked conservatism and sought principled change rather than return.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Inferred: Rand insisted on principles over expediency, but her stance on pragmatism was not opened here.

direct-action.rationale: Unjust laws are opposed through ideas, not martyrdom or force.

means-match-ends.rationale: Inferred from the principle that force cannot achieve a free society and persuasion by reason must.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Objectivism holds reason and production are the means of human survival and flourishing.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Trade among independent producers is central to the trader principle.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rand denies that the need of others is a first mortgage on one's life, and attacks the morality in which need, not ability, gives a claim to rewards.

production-for-use.rationale: Profit is the legitimate reward for productive work.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Value of work is set by voluntary trade, so profit is earned, not exploited.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dictatorship is statism and class rule violates individual rights.

collective-farming.rationale: Rand defines capitalism as a system in which all property is privately owned, so forced collective farming is ruled out, though she does not discuss farming directly in these sources.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rand argued laissez-faire capitalism is the only system that bans force, and so causes peace.

taxation-theft.rationale: Objectivists oppose involuntary taxation and favor voluntary funding of government, though Rand did not call it theft.

harm-principle.rationale: Close to the non-initiation principle: force only against those who initiate force.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rejects collective rights; rights belong to individuals.

conscription.rationale: Rand called the draft an abrogation of rights.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Objectivism relies on rights and objective law, not on exit, as the check on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Government is a monopoly on retaliatory force with limited functions, not a business with customers.

media-academia-power.rationale: Rand stressed the power of intellectuals over culture, but not that they outrank elected officials; not opened here.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Racism is condemned as collectivism; individuals are judged on their own character.

organic-representation.rationale: Rights-based representation of individuals, not group bodies, is the standard.

total-state.rationale: Total state control is the opposite of Rand's position.

national-rebirth.rationale: Rand sought an intellectual renaissance rather than a national one.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The warrior is the antagonist of the trader; only defensive force is legitimate.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule must follow objective law, not personal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Rand writes that capitalism cannot work with slave labour and praises it for wiping out slavery and serfdom, leaving no way to serve one's interests by enslaving others.

universal-morality.rationale: Ethics is objective and applies to all humans because it is rooted in human nature.

single-common-good.rationale: Rand rejected the collective good as a standard; rational interests are individual, not one common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed directly; self-determination only for free nations, with no ethnic claim.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Inferred: an ethnic-group claim to citizenship is a collective claim, though individuals may immigrate freely.

revive-national-language.rationale: Inferred: the state should not direct culture or language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Owners decide how firms are run; majority votes over property violate rights.

school-vouchers.rationale: Objectivists oppose public education, and publicly funded vouchers remain tax-funded.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from opposition to government economic management.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rand held that political freedom requires economic freedom and the separation of state and economics.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule must come from objective, enforceable law, not the moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Free nations alone have a right to self-determination, so the claim is conditional.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred: a free nation need not seek approval from a world body to defend its rights.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Rand held reason is the only absolute and the only source of knowledge, rejecting faith and mysticism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from Rand's rejection of state welfare for anyone and her view that rights belong to individuals, not citizens; the statement's framing fits neither side.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rand defines rights as freedom from physical force, so no one has a claim on others for the means to act.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred: Objectivists reject welfare altogether, so a work condition is at best a lesser evil rather than a principle.

class-collaboration.rationale: Rand held that the interests of rational people do not conflict and rejected Marxist class warfare, favoring voluntary trade between employers and workers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred: Rand valued great art and achievement and opposed sacrificing anything to a collective, but she rejected tradition for its own sake.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism rejects collectivist group claims such as bloc solidarity against nations, and favors free trade with all.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism rejects organizing by class or nation as collectivism, so national class organization is opposed along with international.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Objectivism holds that law protects individual rights and rejects group-based treatment, so legal sex roles are opposed.

ban-interest.rationale: Laissez-faire capitalism protects free contract, including loans at interest, and Objectivists oppose government interference in it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Rand called racism the lowest form of collectivism and opposed any legal treatment of people by race.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Objectivists reject the Marxist class view; the proper state protects individual rights and acts as an objective arbiter.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The Atlas Society presents nature as having no intrinsic value and opposes environmental regulation, so Objectivists favor production of energy by private owners.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Objectivists reject group claims and favor open immigration, but inferred from individualism that culture is chosen, not demanded by the state.

elite-replacement.rationale: Rand rejected collectivism and racism as primitive group thinking, and the ARI supports open immigration, so a plot to replace a native population is rejected.

proportional-representation.rationale: Rand did not address electoral systems and followers are split; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Rand rejected altruistic sacrifice in foreign policy, so a duty to spread a system is rejected, though she praised the US as uniquely free.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Objectivism rejects collectivist group claims and holds that rights are individual, so it denies systematic group advantage as a social structure.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Inferred: Rand held that statist politicians are looters who serve pressure groups, but she did not make elite corruption a theme.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Rights are individual and the state may not initiate force, so state control over procreation is rejected.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred: government exists to protect rights and the law must be objective, so officials who violate rights should be answerable.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rand held the only proper government protects rights through police, armed forces and courts under laissez-faire capitalism.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Rand called racism the lowest, most primitive form of collectivism and held people should be judged by their own character and actions.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Rand demanded equal individual rights for all, but held moral worth is earned by virtue, so the first half of the statement is only partly accepted.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Rand rejected socialism entirely but this is a debate within Marxism that Objectivism does not address.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Rand held that individual rights and property, not group claims or ancestry, decide such cases; inferred, and she was criticized for her remarks on this subject.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Government is bound by objective law protecting individual rights equally, so a single civil law rather than group-based personal law follows.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Only initiated force may be forbidden, and a law policing a peaceful change of belief would itself initiate force against non-aggressors.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Animals have no rights and government may not use force beyond protecting individual rights, so such a ban is a violation of owners.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Rand rejected faith and opposed state compulsion in belief, though she would privatize schooling; the statement agrees with her secularism, so this is inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Government must be limited to protecting individual rights, so a state growing stronger on any pretext is rejected; inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rand wrote that government holds only the powers citizens delegate and that its authority rests on the consent of the governed.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Objectivism holds that reality and truth are objective and knowable by reason independent of who holds power, as for its answer on knowledge-power.

trade-surplus.rationale: Rand defended unrestricted free trade and rejected mercantilist aims as state interference in economic exchange.

population-transfer.rationale: Objectivism holds that rights belong to individuals, so expelling people for group membership violates them.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The non-initiation of force is the central political principle of Objectivism, with force permitted only in retaliation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Rand praised competition among producers but held that interests harmonize and rejected struggle between peoples and Social Darwinism; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Rand opposed punishing ideas, though she allowed action against force; inferred from the limited role of government.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Objectivism defines freedom as the absence of physical coercion by others, not the absence of power to interfere.

separated-powers.rationale: Rand favored a constitutionally limited government, but the sources do not discuss separation of powers directly; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Objectivism opposes collectivism and revolutionary party discipline; inferred from its individualism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Objectivism rejects altruism and holds that no one has a claim on others based on need.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Rand opposed public housing and state ownership, so moving it into private hands is favored, though a statutory right at a discount is not her own proposal; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Rand backed the right to strike as voluntary action and opposed coercive unions, so limits are disliked but force in picketing is not defended; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Rand held that human reason and production create wealth, so population growth does not cause poverty; inferred from her case for capitalism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Rand called racism the most primitive form of collectivism and judged people as individuals.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Government must act under objective law protecting rights, so choosing officials by chance is rejected; inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Government exists to protect rights under objective law, so suspending protections inverts its function.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Rand opposed price controls as force against producers that cause shortages.

party-controls-media.rationale: Objectivists oppose censorship and state control of expression.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces belong to a rights-protecting government under law, not to a party; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Rand favored immigration but gave no settled view on residence periods for citizenship.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from rejection of sacrifice for the public, so officials earn market pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Objectivism upholds individual judgment and rejects subordinating oneself to the collective.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Inferred from Rand's view that governments exist only to protect individual rights, so binding supranational bodies that override them are illegitimate.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from her call for a constitutional government of strictly limited powers with checks.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from rejection of faith and of any state-linked national church.

clerical-rule.rationale: Objectivism rejects faith and mysticism and holds government must be secular and limited to protecting rights.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Rand supported a free country's self-defence and opposed the draft, but did not endorse working for defeat; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Objectivists oppose censorship as government initiation of force against expression.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Rand left no known position on term limits; inferred adherents are split.

recall-officials.rationale: Rand rejected unlimited majority rule and gave no position on recall; inferred as split.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Rand opposed altruistic sacrifice in foreign policy and foreign aid; inferred that government should defend its own citizens rather than maintain entangling commitments.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Property rights are fundamental and capitalism requires free contract, so prohibiting rental is a rights violation.

people-in-arms.rationale: Rand held that government must keep a monopoly on retaliatory force, and opposed the draft.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Rand celebrated cities and industry; no moral ranking of rural life is stated, so this is inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of collectivist and group claims; Rand did not discuss partition as such.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred from the high value placed on reason and intellect and the rejection of anti-intellectualism.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Rand rejected cultural relativism and held that cultures embodying reason and individual rights are superior.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the rights-based view that retribution by the state is just; Rand did not take the issue as central.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Objectivism opposes state-run schooling altogether, so a state curriculum is rejected; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Faith-based accounts of origin conflict with the ideology reason-versus-faith stance, and it opposes state-run schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Objectivism opposes censorship as a rights violation.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Rand rejected racial or group criteria and the ARI backs open immigration; citizenship by descent is inferred to be opposed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state spending on group claims and to coercive redistribution.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from equal individual rights under one law and opposition to religious privilege.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Rand condemned conformity and second-handedness and championed the independent individual.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Rand treated contracts as inviolable and opposed forced sacrifice of lenders; sovereign debt is inferred from this.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Rand held that rights, not a prescribed economic transformation, make a society free; inferred from her defence of laissez-faire.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Objectivism rejects unlimited majority rule and wants government bound by individual rights; a constituent assembly is inferred to be a risk unless it protects them.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Individual rights are inviolable and no goal, including growth, justifies initiating force against citizens.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Rand rejected altruism and the idea that need creates a claim on others; compulsory foreign aid is a sacrifice of taxpayers.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Government exists to protect citizens from force, so a strong independent defence is inferred; Rand did not address nuclear policy directly.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Rand did not address how the head of state should be chosen; adherents care about limits on power more than the method.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Rand favoured separating state and economics and a free-market money system, so a state central bank with a price mandate is not endorsed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Objectivism rejects tribal and collectivist claims to territory, so land claimed as a historic homeland is not sacred; inferred from its individualism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rand held that property is a right of the individual that serves his own life, not a trust for the community.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Rand regarded the USSR as socialist and statist, so calling it capitalist misdescribes it, though she agreed it was an exploitative tyranny.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Rand and Objectivist writers oppose environmental regulation as an interference with production and hold that restrictions need proof of rights violation rather than speculative risk.

collective-defense.rationale: Objectivists back a firm defense of free countries but oppose entangling alliances and altruistic sacrifice for others; the ARI view is split in application.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the stress on individual rights and consent of the governed, which make annexation without consent illegitimate; not directly addressed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Government may only protect rights, so it may not seize church property or control clergy even though Objectivists reject faith.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; Rand's concern is limited government under objective law, not the form of the head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; rights are individual, but a government may defend its legal order, so adherents are split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; Objectivists favor one objective legal system protecting rights everywhere, though freer regions are welcomed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Rand rejects faith and mysticism as sources of authority and holds government must act under objective law with delegated powers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Rand opposed compulsory taxation and favored voluntary funding of government, so a flat tax is only a lesser evil; progression is rejected as redistribution.

character-from-environment.rationale: Rand held that character is chosen through reason and volition rather than determined by environment or heredity, rejecting determinism.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Rand held that government must be bound by objective, constitutional law and has only delegated powers.

space-expansion.rationale: Rand admired space achievement but made no case for expansion as a civilizational goal; she opposed state funding of it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Rand favored a constitutionally limited republic protecting individual rights rather than a blend of class elements; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Objectivism rejects collectivism and the sacrifice of the individual to the state or its leaders; hero worship of rulers is statism.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not addressed in Objectivism and adherents are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Rand rejected collectivism and held that rational interests do not clash; class war and a socialist order are rejected, inferred from these principles.

land-redistribution.rationale: Rights include property, and the government's only task is to protect them, so seizing land for redistribution is forced sacrifice.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed directly; Objectivists would judge by property rights and individual claims rather than descent, so this is genuinely open.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Rand treated racism and ethnic tribalism as collectivism that denies the individual; claiming land for a nationality is rejected.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The state may only protect individual rights and must be separate from religion, so punishing apostasy is forbidden.

women-must-cover.rationale: Government may only use force against those who initiate force, so enforcing modesty rules is a rights violation.

common-currency.rationale: Rand favored money backed by a market commodity, not state currency blocs; inferred, not documented for currency unions.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Rand rejected racial and ethnic collectivism, so unity of peoples by ancestry is rejected.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Rights belong to individuals, not groups, so group-run cultural institutions are not rights; inferred from the rejection of collectivism.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Objectivism stresses individual rights and not group strategy; staying or leaving is left to each person's judgment.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Rand held that ideas and philosophy drive history, rejecting Marxist economic determinism; this is inferred from her stress on reason.

ban-cartels.rationale: Rand called antitrust laws a contradictory mess and held that coercive monopolies arise only from government privilege.

no-bailouts.rationale: Rand's capitalism separates state and economy, so subsidies or rescues of firms are rejected.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Rand held that individual rights limit majority rule, so courts constraining majorities are consistent; inferred from the rights theory.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas treat people as members of groups, which Rand rejected; inferred from her rejection of collectivism.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Rand's capitalism includes free trade and the abolition of protective tariffs.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Rand's free-trade capitalism rejects regulation and the Atlas Society article rejects environmental regulation.

moral-incentives.rationale: Rand rejected altruism and sacrifice, and held that rational self-interest is the proper motive for action.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Rand held that no one may initiate force, which rules out a revolutionary armed vanguard.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Rights and rewards go to individual achievement, so birth privileges in law are opposed; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Objectivists reject collectivist and tribal identities and would privatize schooling; inferred from the rejection of collectivism.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rights are held to belong to individuals, so rule over others in the name of their improvement is not endorsed; inferred, though Rand's remarks on cultures vary.

patriotic-education.rationale: Objectivists reject collectivism and state schooling, so schools should not teach loyalty to the nation as such; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Rand condemned racism as collectivism and opposed racial quotas and preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Rand favored a gold standard and a government separated from the economy; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Rand held that capitalism is just and workable and that crises come from state controls; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Rand opposed altruistic foreign policy and sacrificing citizens to other aims, so cultivating imperial-style influence is rejected; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Rand favored free trade and laissez-faire capitalism across borders.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Rand rejected class warfare and collectivist group claims; wage labor is voluntary trade; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Rand opposed racism but held that government should not force private owners to deal with people, so she opposed such laws for private business.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rand held that government's function is to protect individual rights under a constitution limiting its power.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism treats contracts and objective law as binding and does not endorse group claims of peoples, so it leans against voiding treaties on that ground.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: Rand wanted a government limited by a constitution and run with the consent of the governed, which fits elected rulers over hereditary ones.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected anarchism and held that government must have a monopoly on force, so individuals do not hold a veto over law, though law must be limited to protecting rights.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: Rand held that government exists only to protect rights and defended the American Revolution; a government that violates rights loses its claim to obedience.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred: Rand held that no legislature may violate individual rights, so no body is supreme in the sense of unlimited.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism holds that only rational beings have rights and ranks nature by its value to man, so animal suffering is not a moral claim.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism accepts using animals for human purposes since they lack rights, and treats cruelty as not a moral concern of rights.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Rand condemned altruism as a morality of self-sacrifice, and held that no one owes a duty to the less fortunate.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred: Rand urged rational individuals to defend freedom, and the Ayn Rand Institute engages politically, so withdrawal is not endorsed.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: Rand attacked intellectuals and the press for ideas she rejected, but not as tools of the existing social order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: Rand's 'sanction of the victim' holds that evil rules only with the cooperation of those it rules, which fits power by consent.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Rand held that capitalism produces prosperity and that poverty comes from statism, not from exploitation by trade.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred: Rand condemned racism as collectivism that judges men by birth, which extends to birth-based qualification for office.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism opposes socialism whichever party leads it and has no position on the party's independence.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: Rand opposed foreign aid as state altruism but favored private investment, so on balance adherents are split on the statement as worded.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism permits force only in self-defense and condemns initiating war for collective claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Rand held that rights belong to individuals and condemned racism, which includes granting political rank by ancestry.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred: Rand wanted a constitution limited to protecting rights, not one founded on a political ideology.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Rand wrote that Nazism and communism are both collectivist statism, differing in degree, so condemning them together fits.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred: Rand condemned slavery as a violation of rights and would credit it with causing the war.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism has no position, and Rand would judge each case by the figure's moral worth.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: Rand favored equal individual rights, not group programs, so the statement is mixed.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred: rights belong to individuals regardless of sex, and force by anyone is the same wrong.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Rand held that reason and rights are universal and that a government protecting rights is proper for all men.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Rand held that the military must be subordinate to a government limited to protecting rights, and opposed a political role for it.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: Rand held that work is paid by voluntary trade, so a claim that unpaid family labor should be paid is rejected.

filial-duty.rationale: Rand rejects altruism and unchosen duties, holding that obligations arise from chosen values, though she valued earned family bonds.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism wants a constitutional government limited to protecting rights, with officials not defined as a credentialed class.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Property rights belong to individuals regardless of nationality, so state blocking of voluntary sales is a rights violation.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from marriage as a voluntary association of individuals pursuing their own happiness.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected unlimited majority rule and wanted a constitutionally bound government, not delegates instructed by the community.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Compulsory state pensions are coercive redistribution, and private provision under laissez-faire is the consistent position.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private property in land is a basic right under laissez-faire capitalism, and communal tenure conditional on use is rejected.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the idea that government is a rule-bound agent of rights protection, funded under law.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from opposition to state compulsion beyond rights protection; Rand did not address official languages directly.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Rights are held by individuals as men, not as citizens, so barring foreigners from owning land violates their rights.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Rand held that racism is collectivism and that individuals are judged by their own choices, not group statistics.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Objectivism treats the pursuit of personal values and happiness as the moral purpose of life and rejects asceticism about possessions.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred: Rand opposed sacrifice of citizens' resources to foreign causes, though she backed defense of free nations.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the principle that force may be used only in retaliation against initiated force.

corporate-influence.rationale: Rand held that businessmen seek favors because a mixed economy gives government that power; adherents accept the influence exists but blame state power, not business.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Government interference in voluntary private transactions, including foreign ones, violates individual rights under laissez-faire.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Payments to parents funded by taxes sacrifice some to others, which Objectivism rejects, and it sees childbearing as a private choice.

residents-only-property.rationale: Individual property rights belong to buyer and seller, so a local authority may not bar sales by origin; Objectivist immigration writing treats outsiders' property rights as real.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state-guaranteed job would be a claim on others' production and is rejected as a violation of rights.

democratic-peace.rationale: Rand held that free countries do not initiate force but opposed nation-building and majority rule without limits on rights; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rand held that a law gains authority from protecting rights and that unjust laws should be opposed; inferred, since she also stressed working through ideas and not violence.

non-intervention.rationale: Rand opposed altruistic wars and foreign aid but held that dictatorships have no rights, so an absolute ban on intervention is not her view.

industrial-unions.rationale: Objectivists accept only voluntary unions and oppose compulsion, and have no view favoring industrial over craft structure; inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Rand denounced racism and collectivist group blame as the most primitive form of collectivism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marriage fits as a voluntary contract that the state may enforce, so most adherents would not abolish its legal status; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Government is a servant limited by objective law, which favors open records, though national-security secrecy is accepted; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Rand defended free trade and production for the best price and quality, with no case for local preference.

informal-organisation.rationale: Objectivism favors rational, institutional advocacy and organization such as institutes and parties of principle; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Rand held that only a rights-protecting government has legitimate authority and had no place for supranational bodies, but also denied a state absolute authority; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Rand rejected faith and collective identity as the basis of political life, so defining the nation by religion is rejected.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred from Rand's rejection of the sacrifice of individuals to any collective or power; states should deal as equals under individual rights.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Rand did not address how regions should spend revenue, and her view of government funding by voluntary means leaves the question unclear.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Rand defended private ownership of the means of production as a requirement of individual rights and rejected common ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: Rand was a vehement opponent of communism and of Soviet-style states, and held that they should be opposed rather than appeased.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Inferred: Rand held that government should limit itself to police, courts and the military, so publicly funded services are rejected.

religion-illusion.rationale: Rand regarded religion as irrational faith but did not hold that it fades with material conditions, which is a Marxist claim.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Rand held that capitalism is the only moral system and that its productive achievements are the product of human reason.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected collectivist economic transformation and held that equal individual rights under capitalism suffice.

socialized-care.rationale: Rand's rejection of altruism and of compulsory service means childcare and housework are private matters, not public services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: language policy by government force violates individual rights, which Objectivism limits government to protecting.

treaties-binding.rationale: Rand held that government should protect individual rights, but her view of treaties with internal nations is not stated, so this is neutral.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Objectivism rejects collectivism in all forms, including communities that hold property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred: Rand opposed state coercion of individuals for national or group ends, including state-steered settlement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rand held that capitalism is the moral ideal and that communism is its enemy, so no third way is needed.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Rand rejected rights held by tribes or peoples as collectivism, so a group's ancestral tie to land does not outrank individual property rights; inferred from her case against collectivism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Objectivism's commitment to reason and individual rights treats the Holocaust as a plain historical crime of statism; denial is rejected as irrationalism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Government may only use retaliatory force against those who initiate force, and consenting adults harm no one, so such a law is rejected.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Rand held the state's only legitimate role is to protect rights, so using force against peaceful dissenters or associations is a violation of rights.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Rand was an atheist who held that force may only answer force, so the state may not punish ideas, mockery or religious practice.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial rule for the metropole's benefit is statist plunder; Objectivists favor free trade and no initiation of force by governments.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred from Objectivism's rejection of faith and self-sacrifice: no religious duty can bind everyone to armed action.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Objectivism rejects religion as a basis for law, so a ruler's legitimacy rests on protecting rights, not on religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from Rand's view that government is limited by rights and that majority rule is not itself a source of rights; owners, not collectives, decide in private workplaces.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Rand called racism a form of collectivism and rejected class-based oppression theories, treating each as a separate error of group thinking.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from Rand's individualism: she opposed group-based legal categories and protections, though individuals' rights apply to all.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from Rand's view that each person owns his life and may dispose of it, with contract between consenting adults; she did not address the question directly.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Rand held that both left and right are collectivist statism and opposed compromise between principles, so she rejected blending them.

alienated-labor.rationale: Rand held that productive work is a person's central virtue and creative expression, and capitalism is its proper system.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from Objectivists' hostility to religion as anti-reason; it is not a core Rand position, and Objectivists defend individuals' rights regardless of creed.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Rand was an atheist who held that rights come from man's nature and that reason, not faith, is the only source of knowledge.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from her case for a government limited to protecting rights, which leaves individuals free to dress as they wish, with state schools better abolished.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Rand defended freedom of contract as part of unregulated capitalism, so banning such agreements is an interference.

social-market-economy.rationale: Rand called for laissez-faire capitalism separated from the state and rejected the mixed economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Rand held that protecting the country from foreign invasion through the armed forces is a proper function of government.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from Rand's defense of unequal outcomes earned by productive ability and her view that producers' wealth benefits others.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from Rand's view that a free nation may defend itself and cooperate with free countries; she rejected both statist blocs but not neutrality as a duty.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Rand held that rewards and positions must be earned by individual merit and that no one has a claim by birth, so inherited public office has no place in her system.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: Objectivists favour a fully private, voluntary banking market, so they would not prescribe any one ownership form such as user-owned banks, though nothing forbids voluntary mutuals.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: Objectivists oppose government-to-government lending and the IMF, but they also reject deficit spending, so refusing austerity as such is not their position.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: Rand grounded government in individual rights, not in a property qualification, and did not argue for a property franchise; the source does not discuss the question.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Objectivism treats nature as a resource for human life and rejects the premise that women are dominated through it, and it rejects the collectivist framing behind the claim.

reification.rationale: Objectivism rejects the Marxist account of capitalism, holding that trade is a voluntary exchange between individuals who act by their own judgement.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Rand defended laissez-faire capitalism as protecting free speech, since a private owner's presses are his property and no one has a right to another's means of expression.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rand held that government must act only under objective, publicly known laws applied by courts, and she opposed arbitrary or discretionary rule.

racial-franchise.rationale: Rand called racism the lowest form of collectivism and held that rights belong to individuals regardless of race.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism does not oppose using technology as such, but it does not treat mass participation as a goal because rights are not decided by majority vote.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: A government confined to protecting rights must act under objective rules and be accountable, which favours open records, though Rand did not discuss it.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marriage is a private contract between individuals, and Objectivism holds that the state may not coerce people over faith or voluntary associations.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Rand condemned judging people by group membership as collectivist and racist, which covers shunning shops by their owners' religion.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred from Rand holding that rights are not subject to majority vote and that government should be a narrow rights-protecting agency, so lot-chosen bodies deciding major questions have no place.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Rand rejecting faith as irrational; she wanted reason to replace religious authority, not for believers to reform doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Rand held wealth is earned by production and that the threat to liberty is government force, not private wealth; inferred from her defense of capitalism.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Rand held that rights apply equally to all individuals and the state may not discriminate on private traits; inferred.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The proper government is limited to police, courts and the military, so it may not promote any belief, atheist or otherwise.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Lexicon on government states its proper functions are the police, the armed services and the law courts.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Objectivism treats individuals, not groups, as the bearers of rights and opposes collectivism; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Rand opposed coercive welfare and held aid to be a voluntary matter, but the claim about relative effectiveness is not hers; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by Rand; adherents have no settled position.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed by Rand, who also distrusted unlimited democratic majorities; inferred as neutral.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Rand's limited-government view gives the state no mandate for large collective projects; inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Objectivism rejects religion, but holds religious bodies are private and sets no stance on their offices; adherents have no settled view.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Rand held individuals have equal rights, which cuts against marital hierarchy; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Rand tied political participation to rights under a constitutional government; inferred that voting is a citizen's function, not extended to non-citizens.

rent-control.rationale: Rand opposed government controls on prices and the economy as violations of property rights and voluntary exchange.

abolish-ip.rationale: Rand held that patents and copyrights protect the creator's right to the product of his mind, so abolition is rejected.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Rand opposed the draft as involuntary servitude, and compulsory drilled national service would be likewise rejected.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Rand's support for strong national defence; she did not address basing, and the statement sounds anti-defence.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Rand supported national defence but opposed entanglement; adherents differ on basing, so the sources do not settle it.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: Objectivism condemns collectivist states but rejects group-based guilt and ethnic framing.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Rand held that capitalism rewards productive achievement including the profit and ownership of capital.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Rand upheld the right of self-defence, using retaliatory force against those who initiate it.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from Rand's rejection of racial and ethnic collectivism; she saw it as tribalism.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from Rand's reality-based, reason-first metaphysics; sex is treated as natural.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Rand opposed feminism but also collectivist group categories, so the sources do not settle it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Rand's rejection of altruism and self-sacrifice rules out honouring death for the nation as martyrdom.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Objectivism rejects faith and mysticism, so politics as a spiritual struggle between good and evil is rejected.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected tribal and collective ties, so a nation-wide diaspora centre is not an Objectivist aim.

culture-before-state.rationale: Rand held that philosophy shapes culture, and culture shapes politics, so renewal of ideas precedes political change.

god-not-male.rationale: Rand was an atheist, so the statement is outside the philosophy.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Rand rejected religion as a source of authority, so the statement is outside the philosophy.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Rand called racism the most primitive form of collectivism, so group-reserved economic life is rejected.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred: the philosophy opposes group-based territory in favour of individual rights under a single legal system.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from Rand's capitalism of voluntary association and opposition to government-granted privileges, including compulsory unionism.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: Rand treats socialism as state control of production, so rule by any class does not change that.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Rand limits government to police, courts and the armed forces, leaving all other services to private ownership.

second-chamber.rationale: Rand cares that government protects rights, not how the legislature is organized; inferred as neutral.

municipal-property.rationale: Objectivism defends private ownership under laissez-faire capitalism and rejects collective ownership of any size.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from Rand's rejection of collectivism and of rights being decided by group vote.

family-wage.rationale: Pay by need is the altruist principle Rand rejects; pay follows the value of the work in trade.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Inferred from Rand's opposition to regulation that restrains trade in the name of safety.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the view that government may not tax citizens for purposes beyond protecting rights.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from property rights and privacy under laissez-faire, though Rand expects government to enforce contracts against fraud.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from individualism and privacy; the sources do not discuss the internet.

person-over-state.rationale: Objectivism holds that each person is an end in himself and may not be sacrificed to others or to the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Objectivism rejects faith and mysticism and a spirit apart from reason, although it values consciousness and art.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Rand's concern is that government protects individual rights at every level; the sources do not discuss regional devolution.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from Objectivist praise of technology that transforms nature for human life.

dense-cities.rationale: Rand admired cities, but she rejected the environmentalist premise, so the environmental claim is neither endorsed nor central.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Rand calls racism the lowest form of collectivism, and rejects treating individuals as members of racial groups.

racial-pride.rationale: Rand holds pride must be earned by one's own achievement, and that racial identity is unearned collectivism.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Rand bans initiating force, but Objectivists differ on whether free nations may attack dictatorships.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Rand rejected collectivist group claims; inferred that a shared language does not define a nation over individual rights.

communal-electorates.rationale: Rand opposed collectivism and group-based rights; separate religious electorates would divide citizens by group instead of equal individual rights.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from Rand's opposition to nationalist collectivism and focus on individual rights.

free-public-college.rationale: Rand limited government to police, army and courts and opposed taxation-funded services, so free public tuition is rejected.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Objectivists oppose environmental regulation and see nature's value as set by human needs; a tax on pollution would be coercive.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from rejection of altruism and sacrifice and nature having no intrinsic value; no duty to the unborn is stated.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Objectivism rejects group-based claims and treats individuals as such, so weighting a gender's values is rejected.

arms-reduction.rationale: Rand held government should maintain an army for defense; no position on arms levels is documented.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Objectivists would not clearly favor or oppose secret agreements.

capital-controls.rationale: Rand supported laissez-faire capitalism, free trade and separation of state and economics, so state control of capital is rejected.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Objectivism gives government a monopoly on retaliatory force against criminals and foreign threats, but defends individual armed self-defense; inferred, so it disagrees that all other armed bodies must be disarmed.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Rand opposed the draft and wars of dictatorships but held that a free country may defend itself, so volunteers are not told to refuse; inferred from her views on conscription and war.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Voluntary unions are acceptable but Objectivism opposes compulsory collective bargaining and holds that terms are set by individual voluntary exchange.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Topping up incomes with taxed money is redistribution that sacrifices some for others, which Objectivism rejects.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Objectivism wants a minimal government financed by voluntary means and hostile to deficit spending, so legal limits on borrowing fit; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Rand held that no nation is owed aid or a fairer share and favored free trade under laissez-faire capitalism rather than redistribution among countries.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Objectivism seeks change through ideas and reform toward a rights-protecting government and opposes revolutionary force against a mostly free state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Rand held laissez-faire capitalism to be the only moral social system, not one option among many.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Objectivism values nature as a resource for human life, held as property, so counting it as an economic asset fits though it rejects intrinsic value of nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: Rand rejected collectivism and tribalism, treating the individual rather than the nation as the unit of value.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Cancelling loans forces taxpayers to pay for others' choices, which Objectivism treats as sacrifice and rejects.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Objectivism sees trade as mutually beneficial and rejects group-based exploitation claims; inferred from its individualism.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rand grounded rights in man's nature as a rational being, which supports a fixed basis for dignity.

public-service-media.rationale: Objectivism demands separation of state and economy, opposing government funding of media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Objectivism holds faith and mysticism are false and irrational, so religions do not express any spiritual truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Rand opposed state intervention in the economy, including subsidies and price controls, in favour of laissez-faire.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from Objectivism's view that a government must defend its citizens' rights against foreign threats, so unilateral disarmament would be unsafe.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred from rejection of class politics and collectivism; interests are individual, not those of a class bloc.

ban-fgm.rationale: Cutting a girl's body without consent is a violation of individual rights, which the state exists to prohibit; custom is no defence.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Rights belong to individuals equally, so sex-based limits on owning property are unjust.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred as a factual matter of reason and not of identity politics; Objectivism gives no group claim to a language name.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Objectivists hold that harm to others' property is a rights violation, but favour objective law, and many prefer defined rules over case-by-case suits, so agreement is moderate.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Objectivism rejects tradition and tribal authority as a source of law; government is limited to protecting rights under objective law.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Objectivists reject giving nature intrinsic value over human liberty and oppose environmental regulation that restricts it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the requirement of objective law applied by judges to the facts of each case; fixed penalties ignore individual culpability.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Objectivist-aligned writers favour open immigration with no state conditions beyond rights protection; learning the language is in the immigrant's own interest, not a legal duty.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Rights protect voluntary association and contract, so forcing anyone to join or fund a union violates them; inferred from Rand's rights theory.

voter-id.rationale: Rand's rights theory says nothing specific on ballot identification; adherents would treat it as a technical question.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Objectivism holds the state may only protect individual rights and may not enforce any religion, so no interpretation can have legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Rand attacked unlimited majority rule and held that government must be limited by individual rights, so electoral procedure alone does not make a government legitimate.

premarital-sex.rationale: Objectivism treats sexual choice as a private matter of rational values, not of religious or social duty, and rejects moral bans on it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Rights bar the government from initiating force against peaceful communication and property; shutdowns would violate them.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Objectivism rejects welfare as forced redistribution, and a negative income tax is still a transfer funded by taxation.

women-suffrage.rationale: Rights belong to individuals as such, so women hold the same rights as men; Rand's personal doubts about a woman president make this less than strong.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Rand opposed religion as irrational but saw altruism and the state, not religion, as the main threat to individuals; inferred.

race-social-construct.rationale: Rand called racism collectivism and rejected treating people as members of groups, but she did not take up this question; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Government may only protect rights, so ministries to promote gender equality are beyond its legitimate function.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Rand's view that property rights follow from the right to the product of one's effort; she did not give a first-claim doctrine in these sources, and Objectivists dispute how unowned land is acquired.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred: Objectivists want aggressors punished and reject collective guilt, but distrust supranational bodies that include dictatorships and have no rights-based charter; adherents split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Objectivism rejects faith and revelation as a source of knowledge in favour of reason, so scripture cannot be inerrant.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred: Objectivists reject group-based self-government and tribal rights in favour of individual rights, so the question's framing does not fit; the rights of women follow only from individual rights.

defend-planned-state.rationale: A planned, nationalised economy violates individual rights, and Objectivism holds that such a state has no claim to defence; this is inferred from its rejection of collectivism.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: Rand's concern is a constitution limiting government to protecting rights, not the election method; direct choice is the default in her US-republic model, so indirect selection is mildly disfavoured.

national-church-status.rationale: Government is limited to protecting rights by force, so it may not give any religion privileged legal status; inferred from the Lexicon's account of government.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: Rand rejected ethnic and racial collectivism as a basis for political units, so ethnic autonomy is disfavoured, though local self-rule on rights-based terms is not excluded.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: Rand held that only rights-protecting governments have a claim to sovereignty and that rights are not subject to majority vote, so a plebiscite does not settle it.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Objectivist sources never address colonial borders; the principle that legitimacy depends on protecting rights, not on historical lines, cuts both ways.

simple-living.rationale: Rand celebrated production, wealth and the pursuit of one's own happiness and rejected asceticism as an altruist-mystic ideal.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Objectivists defend free movement and individual rights regardless of origin and oppose group-based entitlements, so restricting settlement for a group's sake is rejected.

equal-conscription.rationale: The Lexicon on the draft calls conscription slavery and violation of rights, so Objectivists would have no draft at all, which satisfies the 'neither' branch.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Rand rejected collectivism, tribalism and mysticism, so a nation's spiritual duty to land is rejected.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Rand held that government may use force only under objective law that protects individual rights, which excludes killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Rand favored free trade but opposed supporting dictatorships; China is a state that violates rights, so this is inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Rand rejected racial and ethnic collectivism, so the state has no duty to kin groups abroad.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Rand upheld private ownership of resources through individual effort and rejected claims of common ownership.

self-ownership.rationale: Rand held each person is an end in himself with a right to his own life, which she treated as foundational.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Rand held government should be funded voluntarily rather than by taxation, which implies abolishing such taxes; inferred.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Rand rejected welfare as forced altruism, so targeting is a lesser form of what she opposed.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Rand rejected rule by collectivist mass movements and leaders; inferred, as she did not discuss this directly.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Rand argued that monopolies exist only through government-granted legal privilege and that government must not give special favors.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Rand rejected faith and religion in politics, supporting a secular state.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Rand rejected tradition as an authority, holding reason alone should guide a person; she admired technological progress.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Rand upheld equal individual rights for women; inferred, as she did not address divorce procedure.

national-resource-control.rationale: Rand upheld individual property rights regardless of nationality and opposed nationalization; inferred.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Rand holds that wealth is earned by production and voluntary trade, so justice lies in how it was acquired and never in equality of outcome.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Objectivism opposes taxation beyond what rights protection needs, and a tax on voluntary trades would be a forcible interference with them.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Rand calls racism a collectivist evil but holds that government intervention and altruism, not private prejudice, now do the main harm; inferred from her view of racism.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Rand held that a government violating rights loses its moral authority, but she did not use natural-law language; inferred from her theory of rights.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Objectivists welcome productivity gains from industry, but would not make working less a social goal; inferred.

multipolar-world.rationale: Rand opposed world government but also had no stated view on multipolarity; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Rand rejects Marx and holds that value comes from reason and productive thought, not manual labour alone, as her defence of capitalism sets out.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Rand rejected nationalism and class politics as forms of collectivism, so an alliance of the two is rejected.

material-over-identity.rationale: This debate within the left is outside Objectivism, though Rand rejected both group-identity politics and class politics; inferred.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Rand rejects socialism and rule by a party as force against individuals, so a market under a communist party does not meet her standard of laissez-faire.

missingStatements.text: Reason, not faith or emotion, should be the only guide to knowledge and action.
missingStatements.rationale: Rand held reason is the only absolute and the only source of knowledge, rejecting faith and mysticism.

notes: Rand rejected libertarianism; the ARI and Atlas Society differ on some points such as open immigration and foreign policy.
